newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil civil service reform faces vote next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil civil service reform faces vote next week.

text.p: A constitutional amendment to reform Brazil's civil service is on course for a first vote in the Chamber of Deputies March 19, a senior whip said.

Deputy Inocencio Oliveira, lower house leader of the Liberal Front Party (PFL), told reporters a special session of the Chamber of Deputies would be called for March 18 to finish off discussions of the bill, allowing for a vote the following day.

The government's civil service reform would allow for the dismissal of currently unfireable public sector workers in state and municipal governments, where payroll spending eats up more than 60 percent of receipts.
It would also set a ceiling equivalent to the salary of a supreme court judge, currently 10,800 reais ($10,285) a month, for the total take-home pay and benefits of all civil servants.

Oliveira said the government hoped to complete voting in the lower house on amendments to a bill regulating the opening up of the petroleum sector to the private sector, which was approved by the chamber last week.
